answer.rationale: The competitor's cut creates pressure toward promotional_pricing, but that is exactly the option my memory warns against: memory_73 records strong acquisition/revenue lift paired with a material 30-day retention drop and an explicit instruction not to generalize it. Discounting into a price war would trade sustainable qualified revenue for a short-lived defensive number, and it would also invite the competitor's third cut. Of the remaining options, only two rest on source records I actually re-pulled this cycle: exp_86 (onboarding, completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, retention +3%) and exp_91 (activation messaging, engagement +11%, activation +6%, retention +1%). Both are confirmed, and both attack the real underlying variable — perceived value delivered per dollar — rather than the price itself. I choose simplify_onboarding because it carries the largest verified retention effect and the biggest time-to-value improvement, and it is independently corroborated by memory_31 on the same SMB self-serve population under pressure. Referral incentive (memory_57) is scoped to established customers, not churning price-sensitive SMBs; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a different segment entirely and does nothing for this week's churn conversations. Important uncertainty I am not papering over: every confirmed result I hold was measured in a non-competitive baseline. None of it was tested against an active price cut, and faster time-to-value may simply not outweigh a large enough discount for the most price-sensitive tail. Onboarding also acts mainly on new and early accounts, so it will not directly retain the existing accounts already in churn conversations — that is a real gap in this plan, not a solved problem. Hence standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout: run it with retention and churn-conversation rate as primary readouts, not activation alone, so we learn whether the mechanism holds under price pressure. Next cycle's budget should go first to re-verifying memory_73's retention penalty, since if that finding is weaker or segment-specific than the consolidated summary implies, a narrowly targeted pricing response becomes reconsiderable; memory_31, memory_57 and memory_44 are consolidated summaries whose original caveats I cannot currently inspect.
